result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.node_percolation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate node percolation by randomly removing nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19315-L19367){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.node_percolation( q, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node percolation](/assets/graphs/node-percolation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: the two diamonds sharing hub D. After removing 30 percent of the nodes at random (here D and F, drawn dashed with their edges), the surviving graph has split into the triangle A, B, C and the pair E, G." width="100%"} Creates a new graph with a fraction of nodes randomly removed, along with all their incident edges. This is useful for analyzing network robustness under random node failures. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fraction of nodes to remove (must be between `0.0` and `1.0`). For example, `q=0.2` removes 20% of nodes. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new Graph containing only the surviving nodes and edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Remove 30% of nodes randomly: ::: {#50110c82 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(10) # Remove 30% of nodes randomly percolated = graph.node_percolation(q=0.3, seed=23) # Returns 7 - number of nodes remaining after percolation percolated.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 7 ``` ::: :::
